_comment: Shared fixture for the push-message whitespace-collapse contract (PLAN-2558 S3).
Consumed by TWO suites that must agree:
len([]rune(...)), the exact pair handlePushToItem applies before its
empty check and its maxPushMessageLen check. That test is the authority;
this table is only true because it passes.
accounting produces the same answers, so an over-length message is caught
in the UI instead of coming back as a 400.
The interesting cases pin the places Go's unicode.IsSpace and JavaScript's
\s DISAGREE: U+0085 (Go: space, JS: not) and U+FEFF (JS: space, Go: not).
A client written against \s is wrong in BOTH directions there, and both

cases.name: plain text is unchanged
empty stays empty
whitespace-only collapses to empty (the server's 400 condition)
newline becomes a single space
CRLF is one separator, not two
a run of spaces becomes one
mixed run of tab/newline/space becomes one
leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed
U+000B vertical tab is whitespace
U+000C form feed is whitespace
U+0085 NEL is whitespace to Go but NOT to JS backslash-s
U+00A0 NBSP is whitespace to both
U+1680 OGHAM SPACE MARK is whitespace
U+2003 EM SPACE is whitespace
U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR is whitespace
U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR is whitespace
U+202F NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE is whitespace
U+205F MEDIUM MATHEMATICAL SPACE is whitespace
U+3000 IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE is whitespace
U+FEFF BOM is NOT whitespace to Go, though JS backslash-s says it is
U+200B ZWSP is whitespace to neither
U+180E MONGOLIAN VOWEL SEPARATOR is not whitespace in current Unicode
an astral emoji is ONE rune, not two UTF-16 units
a combining sequence counts as two runes
a realistic multi-line instruction arrives as one line
